alex.kim: Quick Q — I'll be on a short secondment to Berlin from 2026-06-01 to 2026-07-12. Do we need to run German payroll or withhold DE taxes/social security? I'm a US citizen, paid in USD, no German clients. cc @maria.payroll

maria.payroll: Congrats! Short answer: usually if you're on US payroll and <183 days in Germany, no German income tax, but social security and health can be trickier. Need more details. :info:

chen.tax: A few follow-ups: were you formally seconded by Redwood (i.e., contract amendment)? Still on US contract? Any invoices issued locally or client-facing work? Also, do you currently have any EU social-security certificates (A1 or US Certificate of Coverage)? Germany is covered under US-DE totalization but the certificate is the key.

sophia.legal: Please pause any client-facing work until we confirm — potential PE risk if you're doing sales/contracting locally. Also we need a signed secondment addendum and manager approval for the assignment.

maria.payroll: Action items for alex (please paste into this thread after you submit):
```
- travel dates: 2026-06-01 -> 2026-07-12
- home country: USA
- staying in: Germany (Berlin)
- employer: Redwood Inference (remain on US payroll)
- manager approval: yes (attach)
- client-facing: no
- benefits: remain enrolled in US benefits (yes/no)
```

maria.payroll: Once you submit the "International short-term assignment" form in the HR portal we'll open a case with our global payroll vendor + tax counsel. If the vendor requires local payroll we will need: German tax ID (Steuer-ID) OR work permit info, German bank details for local net pay, and signed payroll authorization form. That process can take 1-2 weeks to confirm.

alex.kim: Thanks — submitting now. Confirming manager approved, internal-only work, staying on US benefits. No per-diem planned.

chen.tax: If there's no A1 / certificate of coverage, German social security could attach. A1 (EU) or Certificate of Coverage (US) shields you from local social contributions while remaining in home country system. Getting that from the US insurer/vendor can take 2-4 weeks, so start early.

sophia.legal: I'll draft the secondment addendum and share in DM for signature. Also flagging export control screening — unlikely but standard for EU travel.

payroll-bot: This thread has been logged. case_id=INT-2468. Assigned to: maria.payroll. ETA: vendor outreach within 48h.

maria.payroll: I'll open the vendor ticket now and loop in our tax counsel. Expect an email request for docs in 24-48h. If vendor says local registration is required, we'll coordinate timing to avoid missed contributions.

alex.kim: Awesome — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
